answer_points: Chemical (enzyme or metabolic) reactions are increased at higher temperatures.
worked_example.question:
Iguanas are lizards. Some species of iguana live on hot islands and use the environment to regulate their body temperature.

A marine biologist measured the oxygen consumption of an iguana at different body temperatures.

Body temperature 20 °C: 0.4 cm³ of oxygen per gram per hour.
Body temperature 25 °C: 0.8 cm³ per gram per hour.
Body temperature 30 °C: 1.1 cm³ per gram per hour.
Body temperature 35 °C: 1.4 cm³ per gram per hour.

Explain why the body temperature of the iguana affects its oxygen consumption.
worked_example.tip: One mark for each link in the chain: temperature, then respiration, then oxygen.

key_idea: Respiration is an exothermic reaction that goes on all the time in living cells. It transfers the energy from glucose that cells need for every living process. Aerobic respiration uses oxygen and makes carbon dioxide and water.

blocks.text: Every living cell needs energy all the time. Respiration is how cells get it from glucose.

items.meaning: A chemical reaction in cells that transfers energy from glucose. It happens continuously in all living cells.
A reaction that transfers energy to the surroundings, often as heat.
The molecule cells use to store and supply the energy from respiration.

blocks.text: What the energy is used for

items: Chemical reactions that build larger molecules, such as proteins.

blocks.text: Plants respire too. Plant cells also need energy for active transport, protein synthesis and cell division.

items: Respiration happens in all living cells, plants as well as animals, all the time.
It is exothermic: it transfers energy, and some of it is released as heat.
Energy is transferred or released. It is never made, produced or created.

blocks.text: Aerobic respiration breaks glucose down completely, using oxygen. Most of it happens in the mitochondria.

Learn the symbols: C₆H₁₂O₆, O₂, CO₂ and H₂O.
Aerobic respiration releases much more energy per glucose than anaerobic respiration.

blocks.text: Cells that need a lot of energy have many mitochondria, so they can respire faster.

items: Heart muscle cells contain many mitochondria. More respiration releases more energy, so the muscle can keep contracting.
Oxygen reaches cells in the blood, and it is used in respiration to release energy.
Glucose also comes from the blood, so a low blood glucose concentration means less respiration and less energy released. A person then feels weak.
Because respiration is exothermic, it also keeps the body warm.
Cells that use a lot of energy have many mitochondria.
Less oxygen or less glucose means less respiration and less energy released.
Always say energy is released or transferred, not produced.
